title: Yielding to a Block knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which approach best demonstrates understanding of “Yielding to a Block”?
options: Replace all built-in features with a third-party framework regardless of the task.
Skip tests because a short example ran once.
Use Yielding to a Block deliberately: state the expected behavior, apply it in a small example, and verify a boundary case.
Assume Ruby automatically guarantees every business rule and external system behavior.
questions.answer_key: Use Yielding to a Block deliberately: state the expected behavior, apply it in a small example, and verify a boundary case.
questions.explanation: Use Yielding to a Block deliberately: state the expected behavior, apply it in a small example, and verify a boundary case. The alternatives overstate Ruby guarantees or encourage unverified behavior.

questions.answer_key: Keep the yielding to a block rule explicit, then test the result against the relevant input and runtime assumptions.
questions.explanation: Keep the yielding to a block rule explicit, then test the result against the relevant input and runtime assumptions. The alternatives overstate Ruby guarantees or encourage unverified behavior.
